words: One that changed recently: US companies and US persons do not report beneficial ownership information to FinCEN; a final rule made this permanent from 14 August 2026.
The habit that keeps this clean in the books: one monthly expense report with receipts attached, reimbursed in a single payment. Do most founders you see run it monthly or quarterly?

Worth adding for e-filers: For tax year 2026, IRIS is the only IRS system for filing information returns electronically; the old FIRE system takes its last filings at 3 p.m. Eastern on Thursday 19 November 2026.
Clear way to put it. Which do you check first before an S corp election: steady profit, or whether the owner is ready to run payroll every month?
And for contractors paid $2,000 or more: Forms 1099-NEC for 2026 payments go to each payee and to the IRS by Monday 1 February 2027, since 31 January 2027 is a Sunday.
Agreed. What goes on your checklist for that review: cash on hand, what's set aside for taxes, or unpaid invoices?
Interesting gap. When owners bring a decision to the table this time of year, is it more often about hiring, pricing, or how much cash to keep in reserve?
Good question to ask. Of the owners you work with, how many found out about the default classification only when the first return was due?
The one-lump-sum trap is so common. Do you move the Profit First percentages every time a payment lands, or on a set schedule? Curious which rhythm stuck for you.
Clear line between an employee and a co-founder. What's your test for a technical co-founder before the equal split: a small project built together first, or conversations alone?
Good tip for small shops. How do you keep an eye on the other states during the year: a quick monthly look at sales by state, or one check at year end?
One change for that year-end list: For payments made in 2026, Form 1099-NEC reports nonemployee compensation of $2,000 or more paid to a payee; the threshold was $600 before.
That receipt hour adds up fast. Do you attach each receipt to its transaction the day you pay, or batch them all at month end?
